text:
sasha: Noticed a regression after merge r3072 — small SSE messages (sub-300B) have p95 up ~20-40ms in staging. Repro with our small-write harness.
neil: any quick reproducer or trace?
sasha: yes, attached perf capture and a tiny harness that pushes 1KB payloads split across frames. CPU looks ok but tails are worse.
kai: I ran syscall traces. Before: 1 write per frame. After: we now have 2 writes per frame in the hot path. p95 +18ms on the tiny-write test. Short trace: 
```
write(3, "event: message\ndata:...\n\n", 128) = 128
write(3, "\n", 1) = 1   <-- extra small write
```
neil: hmm that smells like we split header/body and ended up flushing twice. Which change touched that path?
sasha: commit f3a9e5c introduced a response normalization layer to enforce Content-Length and a trailing CRLF for certain toolcall consumers. It added a separate write in router-proxy.
jamal: CI surfaced this earlier: ci-bot posted a streaming perf failure.
ci-bot: perf/regressions/streaming: FAILED metric=stream.sse.p95 baseline=74ms current=92ms delta=+24%
maya: I also saw a small kv-cache hit-rate dip around the same window. Eviction rate ticked up; might be a side effect of changed backend queue timing.
kai: profiling shows user CPU unchanged, but syscall count and memcpy hot paths increased. Minimal GC/alloc noise. Likely extra syscall + extra copy and TLS record coalescing behavior causing delayed flushes.
sasha: did a short bisect — reverting f3a9e5c locally removes the spike. Bisect points to that normalization path.
neil: can we patch without reverting the whole commit? Options: coalesce header+body into one write, use writev, or adjust socket options (TCP_NODELAY / TCP_CORK) to avoid small writes making it to the wire as separate TLS records.
kai: I prototyped writev in router-proxy and replayed staging traffic. p95 returned to baseline (actually -2ms). No other perf tests regressed in my quick run.
jamal: also the commit added a JSON.stringify for some toolcall metadata on the hot path which costs ~150-300us per call. That explains a small extra latency per toolcall loop. We should remove or lazily compute that.
maya: good to fix both. The extra syscall explains streaming tail spikes and interacts with our batching heuristics: the kernel can no longer coalesce multiple tiny writes into one when we split writes, so runtime batching is less effective.
ci-bot: build/3072: tests=OK. perf/regressions/streaming: still failing at head. rollout: HOLD set by eng-runtime.
sasha: action plan proposal: 1) PR to replace separate writes with writev/coalesced buffer in router-proxy (small change) 2) remove or defer JSON.stringify on hot toolcall path 3) add unit test in stream-harness that asserts single-write semantics for SSE frames 4) run extended perf job on canary and run kv-cache metric checks 5) keep rollout blocked until canary clears.
jamal: drafting PR now with microbenchmarks and perf diffs. Will include the bisect artifacts and syscall traces. Also adding an integration test that uses a raw socket inspector to assert only one write syscall per frame.
kai: note: if we go the writev path, need to ensure fallback on platforms that don't expose writev on our runtime layer (but we have wrappers). Also consider using io_uring batching later.
neil: platform-side option is to enable TCP_NODELAY earlier while SSE is active, but that changes network behavior and might have other perf impacts. Prefer fixing userland writes first.
maya: I'll monitor kv-cache eviction signals on canary; add dashboard for this window.
platform-oncall: Canary hold acknowledged. Will not promote main until eng-runtime clears the hold.
ci-bot: perf/compare will attach results to PR once the job completes.
sasha: TL;DR: root cause = extra write introduced by response normalization path; fixes = writev/coalesce + remove unnecessary stringify + CI test to catch single-write regression; rollout blocked until verification.
neil: agreed. Once PR lands, let's run the long-running perf job (30m) and sanity-check our batching and kv metrics.
sasha: closing the loop here — will post PR link and perf diffs in this thread when available.
